subject: general
question: Which is the biggest coffee producing country in the world?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Brazil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brazil **is, quite simply, the **largest coffee producer **in the **world**.
 
• For example, **in 2016 **it is thought that **2,595,000 metric tons **of **coffee beans **were produced in Brazil alone.
 
• **According **to a story written down in **1671**, **coffee **was **first discovered **by the **9th-century Ethiopian goat-herder Kaldi**.
 
• The earliest **credible evidence **of the **drinking of coffee **in the form of the **modern beverage appears **in **modern-day Yemen **from the mid**-15th century **in **Sufi shrines**, where coffee seeds were first roasted and brewed in a manner similar to current methods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Peru **is the **leading producer **of **alpaca fiber **in the **world**. It is also the **country **with the **largest alpaca population **in the **world**, with more than **3.6 million specimens**.
 
• **Argentina **is the **largest producer **in the **world **of **yerba mate**, one of the **5 largest producers **in the world of **soy**, **maize**, **sunflower seed**, **lemon**, and **pear**.
 
• **India **is the **world's largest **producer of **milk**, **pulses **and **jute**, and **ranks **as the **second largest producer **of **rice**, **wheat**, **sugarcane**, **groundnut**, **vegetables**, **fruit **and **cotton**.
